extraction.name: Visual Genome
extraction.description: A dataset of 108,249 real-world images with crowdsourced dense annotations comprising region descriptions, localized objects, attributes, relationships, region graphs, scene graphs, and 1,773,258 question-answer pairs. Objects, attributes, relationships, and noun phrases in descriptions and question-answer pairs are canonicalized to WordNet synsets to support comprehensive visual scene understanding.
extraction.creator: Ranjay Krishna; Yuke Zhu; Oliver Groth; Justin Johnson; Kenji Hata; Joshua Kravitz; Stephanie Chen; Yannis Kalantidis; Li-Jia Li; David A. Shamma; Michael S. Bemstein; Li Fei-Fei
extraction.citeAs: Ranjay Krishna et al. Visual Genome: Connecting Language and Vision Using Crowdsourced Dense Image Annotations. arXiv:1602.07332v1 [cs.CV], 23 February 2016.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Images were selected from the intersection of MS-COCO and YFCC100M. Annotations were collected and verified entirely by Amazon Mechanical Turk crowd workers. More than 33,000 unique workers contributed through approximately 800,000 Human Intelligence Tasks involving descriptions, question-answer pairs, and region graphs. Collection lasted six months after 15 months of experimentation and iteration on the data representation.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis; Manual Human Curator; User-generated content data
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: All 108,249 images in the intersection of MS-COCO's 328,000 images and YFCC100M's 100 million images. These are real-world, non-iconic images uploaded to Flickr by users. Raw annotations are freeform worker-generated descriptions and question-answer texts, followed by crowd-extracted objects, attributes, and relationships.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: Collection lasted six months following 15 months of experimentation and iteration. Start and end dates are not stated.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Region graphs were combined into one scene graph per image by merging co-referenced objects. Section 4.5 specifies bounding-box intersection-over-union of 0.8 to identify candidate matches, followed by human confirmation before merging; Figure 12 instead states a minimum threshold of 0.9. Objects, attributes, relationships, and noun phrases in descriptions and question-answer pairs were mapped to WordNet synsets. Noun phrases were mapped using WordNet lexeme frequencies with 30 hand-crafted correction rules. Attributes were stemmed and mapped with 15 correction rules. Relationship canonicalization excluded prepositions, matched verb sentence frames, considered root hypernyms, and used 20 correction rules. Workers verified proposed synsets against four alternatives.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Annotations were verified to eliminate incorrect object, attribute, and relationship labels and remove vague, subjective, or opinionated descriptions and question-answer pairs. For attribute experiments, attributes were lowercased, lemmatized, and stripped of excess whitespace; the 100 most common attributes were used, objects had to occur at least 100 times, and up to 500 instances per attribute class were sampled. Object bounding boxes were cropped as model inputs. Relationship experiments used the 100 most frequent relationships, lowercasing, lemmatization, whitespace stripping, and image crops containing the union of subject and object bounding boxes. Region-captioning experiments removed non-alphanumeric characters, lowercased descriptions, stripped excess whitespace, and extracted VGG features from region crops.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Workers initially drew three region bounding boxes and wrote corresponding descriptions. Images were passed to additional workers with existing descriptions until 50 descriptions were collected. Workers were encouraged to describe new content; BLEU similarity thresholds of 0.7 were enforced against existing image descriptions and the 100 most common descriptions globally. Region boxes had to cover every mentioned object. Each description was sent to one worker to extract objects and draw tight bounding boxes, with a four-pixel tolerance for tightness; existing objects and parser-extracted nouns were provided as suggestions. Workers then added attributes and relationships from each description. Descriptions without objects received no region graph. For freeform question answering, workers wrote eight question-answer pairs spanning at least three interrogative types. Region-based pairs used regions larger than 5,000 pixels with descriptions longer than four words. Questions had to be precise, unique, image-answerable, and non-ambiguous rather than speculative. Workers also verified annotations and WordNet mappings.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: Amazon Mechanical Turk (AMT). Object verification additionally used a rapid-judgment interface inspired by rapid serial visual processing.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: All components except objects were verified by three unique workers using majority voting; annotations were retained when at least two workers judged them factually correct. Objects were verified using rapid judgments. Candidate object merges required human confirmation because bounding-box overlap could produce false positives. WordNet mappings were reviewed by workers presented with five synsets without identifying the proposed mapping, to discourage defaulting to it. Canonicalization precision and recall were 88.0% and 98.5% for objects, 85.7% and 95.9% for attributes, and 92.9% and 88.5% for relationships. Evaluation included manually annotated samples of 200 region descriptions, 200 attributes, and 200 relationships.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: Each image has an average of 42 region descriptions and 17 question-answer pairs. Each region description was sent to one worker for object extraction. Each non-object annotation received three independent verification votes. The number of object-verification judgments per item is not stated.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: More than 33,000 unique workers contributed. Geographic distribution: United States 93.02%, Philippines 1.29%, Kenya 1.13%, India 0.94%, Russia 0.50%, Canada 0.47%, and other countries 2.65%. Most workers were 25–34 years old; the youngest was 18 and the oldest 68. Workers were 54.15% male and 45.85% female.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Stanford dependency parser; Stanford NLP tools / Stanford CoreNLP; WordNet for synset canonicalization; BLEU scoring for description-similarity checks.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The paper reports annotator country, age, and gender distributions. Image annotations also include human-related descriptors such as man, woman, boy, young, teenager, and male; an example region description identifies a 'young Asian woman wearing glasses.'
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: Human Intelligence Tasks were designed to allow continuously working annotators to earn $6–$8 per hour, which the authors describe as consistent with ethical research standards on Mechanical Turk. The paper identifies image search, question answering, and robotic interactions as applications of improved scene understanding.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The image set is somewhat biased toward people. Its three most common image synsets—ski, ballplayer, and racket—refer to sports scenes. Humans, animals, sports, and scenery are common object categories, with man, person, and woman occurring especially frequently. Certain sports, including skiing and surfing, are overrepresented due to image-source bias. Common visual elements and colors occur much more frequently than nuanced elements. Relationship frequencies follow a Zipf distribution, and question-answer answers have a long-tail distribution.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: WordNet mappings are not perfect and retain ambiguity. Prepositions are excluded from relationship canonicalization because WordNet does not recognize them. The Stanford dependency parser sometimes misses compound nouns, so object extraction does not depend on it alone. Descriptions without explicit objects have no associated region graphs. Bounding-box overlap can produce false-positive object matches, requiring human confirmation. Region descriptions are short and may be incomplete sentences, making captioning results not directly comparable with full-image captioning. Exact-match question-answer evaluation works well for short answers but causes problems for longer phrases and sentences.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training and benchmarking models for comprehensive scene understanding, object detection, attribute prediction, relationship prediction and extraction, dense image captioning, visual question answering, action recognition, spatial orientation, and semantic image retrieval. Scene graphs can support knowledge representation and evaluation of image understanding by comparing generated descriptions or answers with ground-truth graphs. Attribute experiments used image-exclusive 80% training, 10% validation, and 10% testing splits. Region-captioning experiments kept all regions from an image in one split and used 3,150,000 training descriptions and 504,420 descriptions each for validation and testing. Question-answer experiments used image-exclusive 60% training and 40% testing splits.
